description: An eight-channel step sequencer whose whole pattern is edited on an eight by eight grid: eight groups, each holding eight presets, each holding eight channels of eight steps

params.text: Sets the tempo of the internal clock, 1 to 400 beats per minute, taking one step every sixteenth note; a cable in the clock input takes over and this knob is then ignored

inputs.text: Advances the sequence one step on each rising edge past 1V, in place of the internal clock, and stops the BPM knob having any effect while a cable is patched here
Sets the sequence back so that the next step is step 1 and drops all eight channel outputs to 0V, on a rising edge past 1V, whether the sequencer is running or stopped

outputs.text: A 2ms pulse at 10V on every step the sequencer takes
That channel's step: 10V for 10ms where the step is set to a trigger, 10V for the whole step where it is set to a gate, and 0V where the step is empty or the channel is muted

notes: nothing comes out until the sequencer is started. It comes up stopped: click START at the top right of the panel, or press the space bar with the pointer over the module.
the grid is one widget rather than 64 separate buttons, so no cell of it can be clicked for help.
clicking a step cell cycles it from empty to a trigger to a gate and back, and dragging across cells paints the value the drag started with.
the round button below the grid cycles it between three layouts, and the V key does the same: VERT, 8x8 and 1x64.
VERT puts the navigation in the grid's own columns, 8x8 shows eight channels against eight steps, and 1x64 shows eight presets of one channel against eight steps.
in VERT the grid's first five columns are the controls: the first picks the group, the second the preset, the third holds the eight steps, the fourth picks the channel and the fifth mutes it.
in VERT, clicking the preset already chosen turns on cascade, in which editing a step writes it into all eight presets of the group at once; clicking a different preset turns cascade off.
in VERT the grid's top right corner holds seven toggles: group loop, set loop and preset loop on the first row, copy, paste and clear on the second, and random on the third.
copy, paste, clear and random are armed by one click and take effect on the next: click one, then click a group, preset or channel cell, and it acts on that one.
group loop steps to the next group marked in set loop mode each time the pattern comes round, and preset loop does the same for presets inside the group.
with the pointer over the module the space bar starts and stops it, V cycles the view, and the number keys 1 to 8 mute a channel.
with the pointer over the module, holding G, P or C and pressing a number key from 1 to 8 picks the group, the preset or the channel.
swing is built into this version but has no control on the panel, and the per-channel swing values are only set by loading a saved pattern, so a pattern built here plays without swing.
the module is monophonic: every jack reads or writes one channel.
menu: Random Weighting — a slider setting how likely each step is to be filled when the grid's random toggle is used
Enable Hardware Sync — turns on talking over the network to a Cavian hardware unit, and adds items for loading and saving that unit's patterns
Save Pattern To... — writes the whole pattern, all eight groups, into one of 64 named slots in a folder Rack keeps for this module
Load Pattern From... — reads a whole pattern back out of one of those 64 slots, replacing everything in the module
Manage Patterns — a submenu holding Rename Current Pattern and Clear Slot
